sentences.text: (By Shri Vinod Thakur, Government Advocate)

This application coming on for order this day, th e cou  following:
 ORDER 01.

This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 o f Cr.P.C. as he is implicated in connection with FIR/Crime No.661/2022 registered at Police Station Kotwali, District Mandsaur (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 406, 409, 201 of IPC.

The applicant is in custody since 24.11.2022.
02.

As per the prosecution case, the complainant Vishnu had filed a written complaint on 03.11.2022 stating that, after dated 28.08.2022 the present applicant Rishikant demanded the amount and received total Rs.3,90,000/- from the complainant as a processing fee and consultancy fee to provide loan of Rs.23,00,000/- for business purpose under government scheme of Sant Ravidas Swarojgar Yojna .
But after receiving the aforesaid amount the applicant has not provided loan to the complainant thereby he cheated the complainant.
The FIR was lodged against the applicant.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that he has not committed the offence and has been falsely implicated in the case.
He further submits that the applicant has not criminal past.
He is a private person, therefore, Section 409 of IPC is not attracted in the case.
All other offences are compoundable and triable by Magistrate, First Class.
After completion of investigation, charge- sheet has been filed.
The applicant is in custody since 24.11.2022.
The trial will take sufficient long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that present applicant/accused be released on bail.
04. On the other hand, learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State has objected the prayer and prayed for rejection of bail application.
05. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.

06. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also considering the act of the present applicant coupled with the fact that final disposal of the case will take sufficient long time, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, the application is allowed.

07. It is directed that the applicant- Rishikant be released on bail upon his/her furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his/her appearance before the trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the trial Court during pendency of the trial.

It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
08.
This application is allowed and stands disposed of.
C.c. as per rules.
(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE Shilpa Rishikant @ Chintu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3888762/
